name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with a seat, operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less, in one of three classes: Class I pedal assist to 20 mph, Class II throttle to 20 mph, and Class III pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle or tricycle with a seat or saddle, operable pedals, and an electric motor of 750 watts or less (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-9)
Class I assists only while the rider pedals and stops assisting at 20 mph (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-9)
Class II can be propelled by its motor without pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-9)
Class III assists only while the rider pedals, stops assisting at 28 mph, and must have a working speedometer (South Dakota Codified Laws §§32-20B-9, 32-20B-15)
The motor must disengage or stop when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-11)
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who modifies its speed or propulsion must update the label (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-10)
Class III riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-13)
Class III riders under 18 and all Class III passengers must wear a bicycle helmet; no statewide helmet rule for Class I or II (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-14)
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, title or registration
Class I and Class II may ride on any bicycle or multi-use path unless the governing entity prohibits it (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-12)
Class III is kept off bicycle and multi-use paths unless the path runs within or beside a roadway or the governing entity allows it (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-12)
Class III may ride a nonmotorized natural-surface trail unless the managing entity prohibits or restricts it (South Dakota Codified Laws §32-20B-12)
Only Class I is allowed on the George S. Mickelson Trail, since SB 79 (2025)
